components.role: Unchanged public photo of original 1978 Sten Productions packaging art and folded rulebook front. Kilgor, cracked Alpha crystal, three Imperial relief cruisers and Rebel Hadjidakis identify the matching game. Interior rule pages are NOT present in this photo.

battle-sphere.evidence: Tony Watson’s contemporary Battle Sphere: A Game Review in The Dragon No. 26, June 1979, printed pages 42–43 and46 (PDF 44, 45, 48), successfully retrieved in its unchanged 52-page magazine scan over the site’s working public HTTP URL. HTTPS fails hostname certificate validation; verification was not disabled. The original 1978 Sten Productions packaging/rulebook-front photograph independently matches title, Kilgor, cracked Alpha crystal, three Imperial cruisers, Rebel Hadjidakis and the outer-system setting, BGG 14757. All three article page images were viewed and the complete article read, including its page 46 continuation. This is explicitly a contemporary THIRD-PARTY RULES REFERENCE PDF, not the recovered original publisher rulebook or a newly invented rules reconstruction. The article provides hidden Imperial perimeter deployment then Rebel placement within two perimeter hexes, initial die-selected battlesphere orbit, original three-Imperial versus two-cruiser/one-dreadnought Rebel forces and 21 mines, cruiser/dreadnought/active-battlesphere movement and shot counts, inactive clockwise orbit, adjacent-only coinflip fire, nebula shot reduction, firing before OR after movement, per-turn damage/reset and stated destruction thresholds, mine movement/detonation/chained blasts/friendly effects, crystal transfer and delayed activation/ruses, Rebel escape routes and the 10-point outcome matrix based on battlesphere and Rebel commander survival. It contains substantial concrete rules and final scoring, rather than only theme or product components, and is usable for checking the named summary. LIMITS: the original full rulebook, exact first-player/complete turn sequence, every movement/stacking restriction, all damage combinations and exact edge-case wording are not established by this review. The original physical map and its numbered perimeter/orbit, nebula/mines/black-hole locations are necessary and are not recreated by the article or packaging photograph. No missing rules or board coordinates were inferred from its fictional combat narrative. Selected text retains the complete article, including interleaved fiction, in original column order from exactly documented regions; PDF 48 excludes the separate Thief article. Native text is readable but has occasional source OCR spelling and hyphenation artifacts; original images govern. The unchanged full magazine and separately hashed original photo are retained. One specific MAJOR finding records the summary’s invented automatic victory for destroying the crystal carrier versus the article’s commander/battlesphere point scoring. No full summary audit, PASS or summary-body repair.
